lineage.strategy: Use the changed Grubhub/expansion input to distinguish merchant availability and product breadth from demonstrated utilization and unit economics.

observedWeaknesses.observation: The announcement cites more than 100 participating Grubhub merchants in Chicago and nearly 200 in Los Angeles while also adding cities, hardware, advertising and hospital robotics, but it does not quantify order density, utilization or contribution margin.
observedWeaknesses.whyItMatters: Merchant count and product breadth demonstrate reach, not profitable utilization; simultaneous expansion increases execution complexity.

risks.risk: Breadth across delivery geographies, merchant hardware, advertising and hospital robotics can raise integration and capital-allocation complexity before unit economics by channel are demonstrated.
Merchant availability may be mistaken for demand or profitable scale if order density, utilization and contribution margin are not separately verified.

falsifiers.condition: Subsequent source-addressed operating data show sustained order density, utilization, retention and positive contribution economics across the expanded network.
falsifiers.effect: Would reduce execution and merchant-count interpretation risk.

improvementPaths: Track utilization, orders per robot/day, contribution margin, retention and capital needs by channel as expansion matures.

unknowns.unknown: Incremental revenue and unit economics by new geography/product remain undisclosed.

recommendation: Use as bounded execution/concentration-of-effort risk support without assigning Alpha's numeric risk or score.
